implementation_notes: Ruby intercepts through method lookup rather than a proxy: Module#prepend inserts a module ahead of the class in the ancestor chain, so the module's method can record the event and call super to reach the original implementation - the classic Interceptor/InvocationContext structure becomes prepend plus super. For objects you cannot reopen, SimpleDelegator forwards everything to a wrapped object and lets you override the audited methods, and in Rails controllers around_action is the framework seam that wraps a whole action with before/yield/after semantics. Full transparent interception of arbitrary objects is not idiomatic; audit the named operations.
code_sketch:
module AuditedPayment
  def pay(payment)
    actor = CurrentSubject.id
    sink.record(actor, "pay", payment.id, "attempt")
    result = super
    sink.record(actor, "pay", payment.id, "ok")
    result
  rescue StandardError
    sink.record(actor, "pay", payment.id, "failed"); raise
  end
end
# class Payments; prepend AuditedPayment; end
pitfalls: A prepended module must call super: forgetting it silently replaces the original behaviour, and the class still responds to the method, so nothing fails loudly.
Defining an override for a method the class does not define raises NameError at definition time (super needs an existing method), so prepend-based auditing cannot be added speculatively.
Mixing prepend with framework instrumentation (ActiveSupport::Notifications, around_action) on the same operation records the event twice and hides which layer owns the outcome.
